$comment: SUPPLEMENTAL, NON-GATING. Records the resolution of OI-3. This artifact changes no configuration, no eligibility rule and no threshold. It does not supersede scientific_config_identity.json v1.2.0, which remains active and unmodified.

references.identity_status: ACTIVE AND UNCHANGED. This artifact does not revise it.

open_item.question: Are resid_post and resid_post_all distinct training runs, or one set of runs published under two namespaces with different tier coverage?
open_item.method: Compare params.safetensors SHA-256 for layer_24_width_16k_l0_big, the tier published in BOTH namespaces, at revision 4c419f1ba0be8b7754d4151d4f26c23b92a9029e.

evidence.probe_rationale: This tier is the only one published in BOTH namespaces at layer 24, which is what makes the comparison decisive. l0_medium exists in resid_post only, per OI-1.

interpretation.established: The two releases contain distinct weights. They are distinct training outputs, NOT selective publication of identical weights.

not_established.detail: The hashes establish that the weights are not the same file. They say nothing about whether the difference arises from different training data, a different seed, different hyperparameters, or a different run of the same recipe.
not_established.rule: Record the observation. Do not narrate a mechanism.

effect_on_v1_2_0.what_actually_changed: The EPISTEMIC STATUS of a limit already recorded, not the limit. v1.2.0 prohibited attributing any primary-to-backup difference to release namespace or training artifact, and did so in a way that covered both possible OI-3 outcomes. That prohibition now rests on a demonstrated fact rather than on an unresolved possibility. It neither widens nor narrows.

statements: The fallback is NOT a controlled ablation.
No primary-to-backup difference may be attributed to depth, observed L0, release namespace, or training artifact. Three dimensions move together in Gemma and two in Qwen.
Cross-model matched comparison remains PRIMARY-PRIMARY or BACKUP-BACKUP only.
Qwen TopK k and Gemma observed L0 remain incommensurable; no cross-model sparsity claim is permitted.
Each configuration is judged only by its own independent gates.
No open action remains from OI-3.

rejected_alternative.$comment: The point of recording this. A known-available alternative named and refused is stronger than one left unmentioned, because it closes the 'we did not know it existed' and 'it seemed a reasonable swap' paths.
rejected_alternative.prohibition: MUST NOT be staged, downloaded for experimental use, substituted for the active backup, or reported as an alternative result.
rejected_alternative.why_this_needs_stating: It is a real SAE at the backup depth in the backup width, and OI-3 has just proven it is a genuinely different instrument. If the backup underperforms it becomes an obvious swap. That swap would be post-hoc configuration selection after observing results, which backup_trigger.json prohibits under 'no third SAE family or layer'. Its availability is precisely what makes the prohibition necessary rather than academic.

strengthened_hazard.$comment: Not a new rule. A demonstrated instance of an existing one, which is enforced differently from a theoretical one.
strengthened_hazard.rule_in_v1_2_0: NEVER persist loader_sae_id without its release; the same flat key can resolve to different weights across namespaces.
strengthened_hazard.status_now: DEMONSTRATED. The flat key layer_24_width_16k_l0_big resolves to 774f3026... under one release and ce4e0275... under the other. Same key, same layer, same width, same tier, different weights.
strengthened_hazard.consequence: Any record carrying loader_sae_id without release is not merely underspecified in principle; it is ambiguous in fact for at least this key at this revision.

provenance.gate_proven_by: LA-B, complete v1.2 gate with positive and negative controls
